List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on

Total number of questions—20
85
Size of public holding in a company
*281. SHRI PARMESHWAR
KUMAR AGARWALLA: Will the
Minister of FINANCE AND COMPANY
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that SEBI is in
favour of hiking the minimum size of public
holding in a company from 10 to 25 per
cent;
(b) if so, what are the details in this
regard; and
(c) by when a final decision is likely to
be taken?
Deposits Insurance Corporation for
NBFCs
*282. SHRI DIPANKAR
MUKHERJEE: Will the Minister of
FINANCE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal under
Government's consideration for dealing with
the risks and concerns of the depositors,
whose money is held by the Non-Banking
Financial Companies; and
(b) whether Government would initiate
steps to promote a Deposits Insurance
Corporation for the Non-Banking Financial
Companies?
Carrying of arms in aeroplanes
*283. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of incidents of travelling
illegally with arms etc. in aeroplanes during
last one year;
(b) the names of persons found
responsible for these incidents and the action
taken against them;
(c) whether it is a fact that Government
had decided to send Commandoes in
aeroplanes; and
(d) if so, to what extent this proposal
has been implemented so far?
Foreign exchange earned from
tourism industry
*284. SHRI RAJU PARMAR:
SHRI BHAGATRAM
MANHAR:
Will the Minister of TOURISM AND
CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned
'Foreign tourist arrivals still below pre-
September, 11 levels' which appeared in the
Hindustan Times, New Delhi on 6th
November, 2002;

86
WIN2\SESSION\6139RS 86
(b) if so, the details of tourist arrivals
during the last one year, country-wise/
region-wise; and
(c) the estimated foreign exchange earned
during the last one year from tourism
industry and whether this income is less as
compared to the previous year?
Consultation with States for service
tax
*285. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY :
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of FINANCE AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry of Finance, in
consultation with States, has decided to allow
States to tax some services;
(b) if so, whether the meeting of the Chief
Ministers has been convened by the Prime
Minister to work out the legislative
framework for empowering the States to
tax services;
(c) whether Government have also
agreed to route all the funds to centrally
sponsored schemes through the State
Governments; and
(d) if so, by when final decision in this
regard is likely to be taken?
Financial position of States
*286. SHRI A. VIJAYA RAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of FINANCE AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether many State Governments
are in debt and in difficult financial position;
(b) if so, the details in this regard
including the amount of debt of all such
State Governments as on date, category-
wise;
(c) the details of the steps initiated to
improve the financial position of State
Governments;
(d) whether permission is granted to a
few State Governments for taking loan from
international agencies; and
(e) if so, the details of such State
Governments, international agencies and the
amount asked for and the amount for which
permission has been granted?
Growth of Indian economy
*287. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY :
Will the Minister of FINANCE AND
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether economists have forecast
that the Indian economy would grow by
4.8 per cent as against Government's
estimates of 5.5 per cent in 2002-2003, as
reported in the Economic Times dated the
8th September, 2002;
(b) if so, whether economists have also
warned that if Government does not
accelerate reform process, the country would
not be able to achieve substantially high
growth levels, as reported in the Financial
Express dated the 5th July, 2002;
(c) if so, to what extent Government have
examined these reports and suggestions; and
(d) what steps are being taken to speed
up reforms for higher growth?
Income Tax mobilisation
*288. SHRI S. AGNIRAJ: Will the
Minister of FINANCE AND COMPANY
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that many
professionals like doctors/teachers are not
paying income tax due from them and are
in fact evading tax;
(b) if so, what steps are being taken to
bring them into tax net;

87
WIN2\SESSION\6139RS 87
(c) what steps are being taken to
mobilise more income tax; and
(d) what is the level of achievement of
collection as compared to the budget
estimates so far in this financial year?
Committee on NBFCs

Disaster response team for probing
accidents
1944. SHRI YADLAPATI VENKAT
RAO: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
constitute a national level disaster response
team of experts to ensure that accidents are
probed quickly and impartially and victims
are identified to avoid legal complications at
the time of payment of compensation;
(b) if so, the details of the steps taken in
this regard; and
(c) by when such a response team of
experts would be formed to rush to the site
of accident whenever exigencies arise?
Civil Aviation Training Academy
1945. SHRI P. G. NARAYANAN: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal under
Government's consideration to set up a Civil
Aviation Training Academy in Southern
part of the country; and
(b) if so, the details in this regard?
Palace on Air
1946. SHRI NANA DESHMUKH:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
introduce a "Palace on Air" with seventy
seater aircraft for taking international
tourists to the State of Rajasthan at a cost
of Rs. 1500 crores;
(b) whether Government have assessed
its financial viability;
(c) how much it would cost to an
international tourist;
(d) the details of countries from which
Government anticipate the visitors; and
(e) by when such a project is likely to be
finalized?
N. K. Singh Committee report on FDI
in civil aviation sector
1947. SHRI SATISH PRADHAN: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
the N. K. Singh Committee report on raising
the foreign direct investment limit to 49 per
cent in civil aviation;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Landing of Sahara aircraft on wrong
taxi track
1948. SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news appearing in the
Hindu, Delhi dated the 27th September,
2002 captioned “Private Airlines on the
wrong track;”
(b) if so, the reasons for keeping the
apex regulatory body in dark about
August 10 incident involving an Air Sahara
Boeing 737 on wrong taxi track; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
check such incidents involving Private
airlines especially Sahara and Jet Airways
in future?
Radars at IGI Airport, Delhi
1949. SHRI R. P. GOENKA: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that recently three
out of seven radar display screens, which
monitor the movement and safety of aircrafts
over an air space of 300-350 nautical miles
have gone out of order at the Air Traffic
Control Section of the Indira Gandhi
International Airport and the necessary spare
equipments have not been procured so far;
(b) whether it is also a fact that a poor
substitute, the portable television sets
which can monitor only up to about 25-30
nautical miles are being used; and
(c) if so, the steps taken to replace the
radar screens and also to meet emergencies?
Share of AI in passenger traffic
1950. SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are concerned at the fall in the share of Air
India passenger traffic as several carriers
have captured its large share due to lack of
competitiveness;
(b) whether its share is now just 20 per
cent as against 33 per cent ten years ago;
and
(c) if so, what are the details thereof and
the action taken by Government to correct
the slide?
Second airport at Metro Cities
1951. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
against setting up second International
Airport in or around Delhi, Mumbai and
Chennai;
(b) if so, whether Government have not
yet taken any decision for leasing of airports
to private operators;
(c) if so, what are the main reasons for
not setting up of second International Airport
and also delaying decisions for leasing of
airports to private operators;
(d) whether this project is pending for
long; and
(e) whether Government have now
finally decided to complete the process by
the end of this year?
Profit earned by AI
1952. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Air India has registered a

year; and
(b) if so, the amount of profit and the

Eligibility for Haj subsidy

MISS MABEL REBELL
